extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and physicists (readers/students of classical celestial mechanics and conic-section geometry)
extracted.subtask_description: Geometric and dynamical rules for orbits (conic sections) under centripetal forces: lemmas, propositions and constructions relating latus rectum, distances, velocities, periods, and explicit construction methods to obtain conic trajectories from given data (umbilicus, points, tangents, axes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse-square centripetal force
rubrics_metrics.description: vis centripeta reciproce est ut ... reciproce in duplicata ratione distantiae SP (i.e., the centripetal force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance SP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly (propositions and corollaries) to deduce that under an inverse-square centripetal force a body moves in a conic section about the center of force; used to derive velocity relations, latus-rectum relations, period laws, and to construct orbits given initial conditions. Corollary: converse holds — given conic curvature and velocity one recovers the inverse-square law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latus rectum of parabola relative to umbilicus
rubrics_metrics.description: Latus rectum parabolae ad verticem quemvis pertinens est quadruplum distantiae verticis illius ab umbilico figurae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric relation from conic theory: for a parabola the latus rectum through any vertex equals four times the distance from that vertex to the umbilicus. Used in later constructions and to relate ordinates and tangents (lemma XIII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpendicular from umbilicus to tangent is mean proportional
rubrics_metrics.description: Perpendiculum, quod ab umbilico parabolae ad tangentem ejus demittitur, medium est proportionale inter distantias umbilici a puncto contactus & a vertice principali figurce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma XIV: If SN is the perpendicular from the focus/umbilicus to the tangent at the contact point P, then SN is the mean proportional between distances from the umbilicus to the contact point and to the principal vertex. Corollaries give algebraic relations (PS^2 related to SN^2 and SA) used to compute perpendiculars and thereby velocities for parabolic motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centripetal law for motion on a parabola
rubrics_metrics.description: Moveatur corpus in perimetro parabolae: requiritur lex vis centripeta tendentis ad umbilicum hujus figurae ... vis centripeta est reciproce ut SP^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition XIII: A body constrained to move on a parabola with the centripetal force directed to the umbilicus experiences a centripetal acceleration inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the umbilicus. Supports identification of inverse-square force law from parabolic orbit geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conic orbits ↔ inverse-square force equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpus ... vi centripeta, quae sit reciproce proportionalis quadrato distantiae locorum a centro, simul agitetur; movebitur hoc corpus in aliqua sectionum conicarum umbili cum habente in centro virium; & contra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary to Prop. XIII: If the centripetal force is inverse-square the orbit is a conic section centered on the force center; conversely, given a conic curvature and suitable velocity data one infers the inverse-square centripetal law. Practical consequence: specifying center, contact point and tangent determines the conic orbit for inverse-square forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latus rectum proportional to square of swept area (duplicate ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Latus rectum L aequale est quantitati QT^2/QR quae ultimo fit ... linea minima QR dato tempore est ut vis centripeta generans, hoc est reciproce ut SP^2. Ergo L est in duplicata ratione areae QT x SP (i.e., L in duplicate ratio of area described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition XIV: For bodies revolving around a common center under inverse-square centripetal force, the principal latus rectum of each orbit is in the duplicate (square) ratio of the areas swept by the radius vectors in the same time. Used to relate orbital shape (latus rectum) with area rates and to derive scaling relations for families of orbits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period law for ellipses (Kepler's 3rd law)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tempora periodica in ellipsibus sunt in ratione sesquiplicata majorum axium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition XV: The periodic times of motion in ellipses are in the sesquiplicate (3/2 power) ratio of the major axes (i.e., T ∝ a^{3/2}). Corollary: periods in ellipses equal those in circles whose diameters equal the ellipses' major axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Velocity relation via perpendicular to tangent and latus rectum
rubrics_metrics.description: Velocitates corporum ... sunt in ratione composita ex ratione perpendiculorum inverse, & subduplicata ratione laterum rectorum directe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition XVI: The velocity of a body at a point on a conic orbit is governed by a compound ratio: inversely proportional to the perpendicular from the umbilicus to the tangent at that point, combined with a direct subduplicate (square-root) dependence on the principal latus rectum. Multiple corollaries specialize to maxima/minima distances, parabolic and hyperbolic cases, and compare velocities with circular motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Velocity at extrema: inverse distance & subduplicate latus-rectum
rubrics_metrics.description: Velocitates corporum, in maximis & minimis ab umbilico communi distantis, sunt in ratione composita ex ratione distantiarum inverse, & subduplicata ratione laterum rectorum principalium directe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary to Prop. XVI: At apocenter/pericenter (max/min distances), the velocity ratio between orbits depends inversely on distance from the center and directly on the square-root of the principal latus rectum; useful for comparing speeds at extremal points and transforming between conic and circular cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabola velocity: reciprocal subduplicate of distance
rubrics_metrics.description: In parabola velocitas est reciproce in subduplicata ratione distantiae corporis ab umbilico figurae; in parabola velocitas ubique aequalis est velocitati corporis revolventis in circulo ad dimidiam distantiam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollaries of Prop. XVI: For parabolic motion the speed varies as the reciprocal of the square-root of the distance from the focus (umbilicus). A parabolic orbit's speed at any distance equals the speed of a circular orbit at half that distance (useful identity for comparisons and constructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbit classification by latus rectum and initial velocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Si latus rectum L minus fuerit quam 2SP+2KP, figura erit ellipsis; si aequale fuerit 2SP+2KP, figura erit parabola; si maius, figura erit hyperbola (classification of orbit from given initial speed/geometry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition XVII: Given inverse-square centripetal force and known absolute magnitude, the type of conic (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) described by a body leaving point P with given speed along a given line is determined by comparison of the orbit's latus rectum to the linear combination 2SP+2KP (quantities computed from geometry and speed). This provides a direct decision rule for orbit shape from initial conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superposition and perturbation method for predicting future orbit
rubrics_metrics.description: Componendo proprium corporis motum cum motu illo, quem impulsus solus generaret, habebitur motus quocum corpus de dato impulsus loco, secundum rectam positione datam, exibit; et si vis extra impressa continuo perturbetur, innotescet cursus quam proxime colligendo mutationes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition XVII corollaries & scholium: One may determine the subsequent orbit after an impulse by composing motions (the body's intrinsic motion plus that produced by the impulse), and approximate continuous perturbations by summing discrete induced changes — a method for handling impulsive and small external perturbations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of an ellipse/hyperbola through point and tangent (given umbilicus & principal axis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Datis umbilico & axibus principalibus describere trajectorias ellipticas & hyperbolicas quae transibunt per puncta data, & rectas positione datas contingent: construct circles with centers chosen by AB ± SP and take their common intersection with umbilici S,H and given axis to describe the trajectory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition XVIII: Prescribes explicit geometric construction: given umbilicus S and principal axis length AB, for ellipse use AB - SP, for hyperbola AB + SP to set the radius of a circle centered at P; repeat to obtain a second circle; intersection determines other umbilicus H and the conic. This is a practical construction algorithm to obtain conic orbits through a point with a given tangent/axis data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of parabola from umbilicus, point and tangent
rubrics_metrics.description: Circa datum umbilicum trajectoriam parabolicam describere: Centro P intervallo P S describe circulum FG; ab umbilico ad tangentem demitte perpendicularem S T & produc eam ad F ut sit T V aequalis T S; biseca SI in A' & axe S K vertex K describatur parabola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition XIX: Step-by-step geometric construction for the parabola through a given point P tangent to a given line TR with focus S: draw circle centered at P with radius PS, drop perpendicular from S to tangent and extend to construct auxiliary points, then set the axis via a bisector and draw the parabola. Lemma XIV supports the perpendicular-mean-proportional relation used here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction methods for conic of given species through two points or tangent two lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Circa datum umbilicum trajectoriam quamvis specie datam describere ... (cases): given two points, given two tangents, or one point and one tangent — provide procedures involving constructing circles about given centers, producing perpendiculars, bisecting, and choosing axes so that the resulting conic has the given species and passes through the required points or tangents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition XX: Multiple case-based construction recipes: (Case 1) for two points, set radii proportional to axis-to-umbilicus ratio and use circle intersections; (Case 2) for two tangents, produce perpendiculars to tangents and bisect to set axes; (Case 3) for a tangent at a given point, similar construction. Each case ensures the species (ellipse/parabola/hyperbola) by comparing axis length to umbilicus distances; used for designing orbits with specified constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma for finding fourth point from three given points/line differences
rubrics_metrics.description: A datis tribus punctis ad quartum non datum inflectere tres rectas quarum differentice vel dantur vel nullcB sunt: gives constructions (via hyperbolas/intersections/circles) to locate the fourth point depending on whether linear differences are given or lines are prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma XVI: Practical construction lemma: when three points are given and a fourth point must be located so that three assigned lines have given difference relations, one constructs auxiliary hyperbolas or uses circle intersections to determine the location. Gives multiple cases (differences given, two lines given, all three lines given). Useful as a geometric subroutine in later conic constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding other umbilicus given umbilicus, point and tangent
rubrics_metrics.description: Trajectoriam circa datum umbilicum describere, & inveniendus sit umbilicus alter H: ad tangentem demitte perpendiculum S T & produc idem ad V ut sit T V aequalis S T; erunt V H sequalis axi principali et SP differentia inter H P & axem principalem; habitis umbilicis una cum axis longitudine habetur trajectoria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition XXI: To find the second focus/umbilicus H when one focus S, a point P, and a tangent TR are given: drop perpendicular from S to TR, extend so that the external segment equals the perpendicular, use that point to set the principal axis length and thereby determine H. This gives an explicit geometric way to locate the conjugate focus and hence the full conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trapezium/rectangle-product tangent criterion for conics
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma XVII–XVIII: If from a point P to the four sides of a (possibly infinite) trapezium lines PQ,PR,PS,PT are drawn in given angles, then the rectangle PQ×PR is to PS×PT in a given ratio; conversely, if PQ×PR : PS×PT has the given ratio, then the point P lies on the conic section tangent to the trapezium's sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemmas XVII–XVIII (and corollary): Provide a purely projective-like algebraic criterion for a point to lie on a conic tangent to four given lines: equality (or given ratio) of products of segment lengths to opposite sides. The lemmas give three cases (parallels, non-parallels, arbitrary inclinations) and show the converse: meeting the product-ratio condition implies tangency of the constructed conic. These are used to identify/construct conics from tangency conditions.
